subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should Telegram/outbound media get a dedicated `mediaLocalRoots` config surface, should this be folded into a shared `tools.fs.roots` policy, or should the current managed roots plus file-read policy remain the supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes the public config surface and host file-read/upload authority, and it overlaps the broader open filesystem-roots PR.

options.title: Unify Under One Root Policy
options.body: Define a shared policy such as `tools.fs.roots` or a narrower shared media-root contract and make Telegram consume that instead of adding a channel-specific escape hatch.

options.title: Add Telegram-Specific Roots
options.body: Expose `channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots` with strict validation, docs, and Telegram proof while accepting future consolidation risk.

options.title: Keep Managed Roots Only
options.body: Decline new configurable roots for now and document staging into managed media/workspace paths as the supported security boundary.

recommendation.title: Unify Under One Root Policy
recommendation.body: Define a shared policy such as `tools.fs.roots` or a narrower shared media-root contract and make Telegram consume that instead of adding a channel-specific escape hatch.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the current shared outbound media access policy and the Telegram/outbound delivery surface where this history is strongest.
